title: Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving
technique: Runtime rescheduling across vLLM instances via live KV-cache migration, with a unified 'virtual usage'/freeness-based policy for load balancing, de-fragmentation, priorities, and auto-scaling

optimized_metrics.evidence: Llumnix's scheduling policy is designed with the following goals. The first is to improve prefill and decode latencies, by reducing queuing delays, preemptions, and interference.
Llumnix's scheduling policy is designed with the following goals. The first is to improve prefill and decode latencies, by reducing queuing delays, preemptions, and interference.
Requests with higher scheduling priorities will get scheduled earlier to reduce their queuing delays.

The second goal is load-adaptivity to handle varying cluster load and improve cost efficiency ... instance auto-scaling to keep appropriate cluster load for both saving costs and maximizing the benefits of rescheduling.

headline_claim.text: Llumnix improves tail latencies by an order of magnitude, accelerates high-priority requests by up to 1.5×, and delivers up to 36% cost savings while achieving similar tail latencies, compared against state-of-the-art LLM serving systems.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We focus on request latency, in terms of end-to-end, prefill (that of the first generated token), and decode (that since first generated token to the last, averaged over all generated tokens). We report both mean and P99 values.
metric_definitions.notes: Prefill latency = TTFT and includes queueing; decode latency = TPOT (averaged over all generated tokens), not per-token TBT

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The prefill latency determines how long it takes to start receiving the response, which can be dominated by the queuing delay.
The decode latency determines the speed of receiving the following tokens subsequently.
Llumnix introduces near-zero downtime that is constant to the sequence length
metric_definitions.notes: stall time a migrated request experiences during live migration

slo_spec: No numeric SLO attainment; priorities (scheduling and execution) express differing SLOs; autoscaling targets a P99 prefill latency (about 5 s, red dashed line in Fig 15) while minimizing instances
load_regime: request-rate sweep with Poisson and Gamma arrivals (varying CV), varying length distributions (ShareGPT, BurstGPT, generated long-tail), 16 instances
tradeoff_acknowledged: Migration copy adds up to ~1% slowdown to running batches on the source instance; migration/rescheduling benefits limited under very high or very low cluster load
hardware: 16 NVIDIA A10 (24 GB) GPUs (4 per node, PCIe 4.0)
workloads: ShareGPT (GPT4), BurstGPT, generated power-law/long-tail length distributions
extractor_notes: Tail focus: mean and P99 both reported; headline gains are on P99. Decode latency is a per-request average over generated tokens (TPOT-like), with P99 taken across requests.
